text: In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, 'New test' is defined as qualification tests per Section 4.1, establishing the standard for new testing requirements in qualification scenarios.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the supplier is obligated to meet user requirements for product or process change notifications as part of the requalification framework.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, sample sizes for qualification testing or generic data submission must align with Table 2's minimums and acceptance criteria; generic data should first be used to satisfy requirements before part-specific testing.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the document references other standards, noting that tests A4A and A4Aalt are not executed on Cu wire bonded products, and instead, the requirements in AEC-Q006 must be followed, which also applies to parts being qualified with Cu wire.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Revision E, dated March 1, 2021, was another complete revision that revised numerous sections including 1.2.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.4, 1.3.1, 1.3.3, 2.2, and sections 2.4 to 2.7.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods, TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS, STRESS:Highly Accelerated Stress Test, ABV:HAST, #:A2, DATA TYPE:1, NOTES:D_G1U_V_3, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3 Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-A-110, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:96 hours at TA=130°C/85%RH, or 264hrs TA=110°C/85%RH with part reverse bias at 80% of rated voltage up to a voltage above which arcing in the chamber will likely occur (typically 42V). TEST before and after HAST.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Section 1.2.4 was created to address Decommissioned Reference Documents, specifically guiding the removal of AEC-Q100-003 (Machine Model ESD) due to industry obsolescence and AEC-Q100-006 (Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage) due to lack of industry need.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP E - ELECTRICAL VERIFICATION TESTS includes table header fields: STRESS, ABV, #, NOTES, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT, NUMBER OF LOTS, ACCEPT CRITERIA, TEST METHOD, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the generation of a mission profile is explained. It involves adding detailed information on thermal, electrical, mechanical, and other forms of loading under use conditions to the basic lifetime characteristics, with examples of their relation to test conditions shown in Table A7.1.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP G - CAVITY PACKAGE INTEGRITY TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Package Drop, its ABV is DROP, # is G5, NOTES is H, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is 5, NUMBER OF LOTS is 1, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is —, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Drop part on each of 6 axes once from a height of 1.2m onto a concrete surface. This test is for MEMS cavity devices only. TEST before and after DROP at room temperature.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the legend for Table 2 includes Note H, specifying that tests numbered 16 through 19 are required only for hermetic packaged parts and are performed sequentially to evaluate the mechanical integrity of packages with internal cavities.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the legend for Table 2 includes Note D, identifying certain tests as destructive, meaning parts cannot be reused for qualification or production after testing.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, it is stated that prior qualification data from a part in a specific family can be extended to subsequent parts in that family, provided the supplier ensures no process changes have occurred.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the copyright notice indicates the document may be downloaded free of charge but not resold, is printed in the U.S.A., and can be freely reprinted with the copyright notice but cannot be changed without AEC Component Technical Committee approval.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the document includes a series of attachments designated AEC-Q100-001 through AEC-Q100-012, which are specific test method standards, such as AEC-Q100-001 for Wire Bond Shear Test and AEC-Q100-011 for Charged Device Model (CDM) ESD Test.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, final authority and a key restriction on generic data are established. The user(s) retain final authority on accepting generic data in place of specific part test data. Furthermore, electrical characterization against the individual user part specification is mandatory for each part submission; generic characterization data is expressly not allowed.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, note U allows, for specific tests only, the qualification of a new die in an equivalent package (e.g., DPAK) using an unformed leaded package (e.g., IPAK), provided the die size falls within the qualified range for the target package.

Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP G - CAVITY PACKAGE INTEGRITY TESTS includes table header fields: STRESS, ABV, #, NOTES, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT, NUMBER OF LOTS, ACCEPT CRITERIA, TEST METHOD, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Table 2: Qualification Test Methods, TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS includes table header fields: STRESS, ABV, #, NOTES, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT, NUMBER OF LOTS, ACCEPT CRITERIA, TEST METHOD, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, for broad changes involving multiple attributes like site, materials, or processes, Section 2.3 is referenced, allowing the selection of worst-case test vehicles to cover all possible permutations.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, if a part fails the acceptance criteria, the supplier must determine the root cause, implement corrective actions, and verify their effectiveness; the part cannot be considered qualified until this process is complete and the user is assured the failure mechanism is contained.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Appendix 6 warns that for certain part designs, especially those with green compound molding, etching with red fuming nitric acid and sulfuric acid at high temperatures can damage aluminum wires and pads of 5 mils or less, necessitating careful etchant selection.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS (continued), STRESS:Temperature Cycling Hot Test, ABV:TCHT, #:A4a, DATA TYPE:1, NOTES:D1G1U112, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-A-104 Appendix 6, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:125°C TEST after TC using PV-determined limits at hot, followed by decap and wire pull (Test C3 WBP) on all wires from 5 devices per appendix 6 for parts with internal bond wire sizes 5 mil diameter and less. (Samples may be a sub set of test A4).

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP C - PACKAGE ASSEMBLY INTEGRITY TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Wire Bond Pull Strength, its ABV is WBP, # is C3, DATA TYPE is 3, NOTES is D⊥G⊥E, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT is 10 bonds from min of 5 parts, NUMBER OF LOTS is 10 bonds from min of 5 parts, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is MIL-STD-750-2 Method 2037 for Au and Al wire AEC Q006 for Cu wire, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Condition C or D. For Au wire diameter >1mil, minimum pull strength after TC = 3 grams. For Au wire diameter <1mil, refer to MIL-STD-750-2 Method 2037 as a guideline for minimum pull strength. For Au wire diameter <1mil, wire bond pull shall be performed with the hook over the ball bond and not at mid-wire.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Pb-Free processing typically requires higher board attach temperatures for solder joint quality, which may adversely affect moisture sensitivity, potentially necessitating more robust mold compounds.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the purpose of Appendix 6 is defined as providing a guideline for opening plastic packaged devices to enable reliable wire pull or bond shear testing, specifically intended for use after temperature cycle testing or for bond shear evaluation.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the supplier must provide a Certificate of Design, Construction and Qualification (Appendix 2), Stress Test Qualification data (Table 2 & Appendix 4), and data on the fault grading level of qualification software per Q100-007 for each new device qualification.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, it is specified that all parts, both before and after stress testing, must be tested for their electrical characteristics as defined in the individual user's part detail specification, and these tests must be conducted at room temperature.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP C - PACKAGE ASSEMBLY INTEGRITY TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Wire Bond Pull, its ABV is WBP, # is C2, NOTES is H, P, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is 30 bonds from a minimum of 5 devices, NUMBER OF LOTS is 30 bonds from a minimum of 5 devices, ACCEPT CRITERIA is CPK>1.67 or 0 Fails after TC (test #A4), TEST METHOD is MIL-STD883 Method 2011 AEC Q003, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Condition C or D. For Au wire diameter ≥1mil, minimum pull strength after TC = 3 grams. For Au wire diameter <1mil, refer to Figure 2011-1 in MIL-STD-883 Method 2011 as a guideline for minimum pull strength. For Au wire diameter <1mil, wire bond pull shall be performed with the hook over the ball bond and not at mid-wire.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, specific test method attachments are cataloged, such as AEC-Q101-001 for the Human Body Model Electrostatic Discharge Test and AEC-Q101-006 for Short Circuit Reliability Characterization of Smart Power Devices for 12V Systems.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP E - ELECTRICAL VERIFICATION TESTS (CONTINUED) of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Lead (Pb) Free, its ABV is LF, # is E12, NOTES is L, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is See Test Method, NUMBER OF LOTS is See Test Method, ACCEPT CRITERIA is See Test Method, TEST METHOD is AEC Q005, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Applicable to ALL Pb-free devices. Note the recommendations for all related solderability, solder heat resistance and whisker requirements.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Section A7.3 states that two flow charts are available to facilitate reliability capability assessment for both Tier 1 users and Component Manufacturers, addressing scenarios where standard qualification may need augmentation based on mission profiles.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, a note clarifies that all electrical testing before and after qualification stresses, including pre-conditioning, must be performed to the limits in the individual user specification at room temperature, or the supplier's standard specification limits for generic qualifications.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the Metallization is detailed by its material, thickness range, and number of levels, and the Passivation process is defined by steps like passivation oxide opening, along with its material and thickness range.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Appendix 7 references key industry documents. These include the SAE J1879/J1211/ZVEI Handbook for Robustness Validation of Semiconductor Devices in Automotive Applications and the JEDEC JEP122 standard on Failure Mechanisms and Models for Semiconductor Devices.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, note V specifies that for bi-directional Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) devices, the test duration must be split equally, with one-half performed in each direction.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS (continued) of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Intermittent Operational Life, its ABV is IOL, # is A5, DATA TYPE is 1, NOTES is D1G1P1T1U1W1, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT is 77, NUMBER OF LOTS is 3Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is MIL-STD-750 Method 1037, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Tested per duration indicated in Table 2A. TA=25°C. Parts powered to insure ΔTJ≥100°C (not to exceed absolute maximum ratings). TEST before and after IOL as a minimum. See Section 2.4 for RDSon pass/fail limits.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, note N defines a test as nondestructive, allowing tested parts to be subsequently used to populate other qualification tests or even for production purposes, which optimizes component usage.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a new Appendix 7 – Guideline on Relationship of Robustness Validation to AEC-Q100 has been added, containing explanatory text, new Figures A7.1 & A7.2, and a new Table A7.1 to illustrate the relationship.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP E - ELECTRICAL VERIFICATION TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is External Visual, its ABV is EV, # is E0, DATA TYPE is 1, NOTES is G⊥N, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT is All qualification parts submitted for testing, NUMBER OF LOTS is All qualification parts submitted for testing, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is JEDEC JESD22-B101, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is Inspect part construction, marking and workmanship.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, references for applying the assessment method are provided, including SAE J1879, SAE J1211, and the ZVEI Handbook for Robustness Validation of Semiconductor Devices in Automotive Applications.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, two flow charts facilitate assessment: Flow Chart 1 for Component Manufacturers qualifying new parts, and Flow Chart 2 for Tier 1s assessing components for new ECUs or for using qualified parts in new applications, leading to conclusions [A], [B], or [C].

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP G - CAVITY PACKAGE INTEGRITY TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Variable Frequency Vibration, its ABV is VFV, # is G2, NOTES is H, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is 15, NUMBER OF LOTS is 1, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is JEDEC JESD22-B103, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is 20 Hz to 2 KHz to 20 Hz (logarithmic variation) in >4 minutes, 4X in each orientation, 50 g peak acceleration. TEST before and after at room temperature.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 2.5, which defines a Test Failure After Stressing, has been updated with a new statement concerning Electrical Overstress (EOS) conditions.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, it is stipulated that parts exceeding the defined failure criteria require justification from the supplier and approval from the user; failures agreed to be due to mishandling or ESD are to be discounted but must still be reported in the data submission.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP E - ELECTRICAL VERIFICATION TESTS, STRESS:Electrostatic Discharge Charged Device Model, ABV:CDM, #:E3, NOTES:H, P, B, D, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:See Test Method, NUMBER OF LOTS:1, ACCEPT CRITERIA:Target: 0 Fails 750V corner pins, 500V all other pins (Classification C4B or better), TEST METHOD:AEC Q100-011, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:TEST before and after ESD at room and hot temperature. Device shall be classified according to the maximum withstand voltage level. Device levels <750V corner pins and/or <500V all other pins CDM require specific user approval. Refer to Section 1.3.1.

In TEST GROUP D - DIE FABRICATION RELIABILITY TESTS (CONTINUED) of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Stress Migration, its ABV is SM, # is D5, NOTES is —, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is —, NUMBER OF LOTS is —, ACCEPT CRITERIA is —, TEST METHOD is —, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is The data, test method, calculations and internal criteria should be available to the user upon request for new technologies.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP C - PACKAGE ASSEMBLY INTEGRITY TESTS, STRESS:Wire Bond Shear, ABV:WBS, #:C1, NOTES:H, P, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:30 bonds from a minimum of 5 devices, NUMBER OF LOTS:30 bonds from a minimum of 5 devices, ACCEPT CRITERIA:CPK>1.67, TEST METHOD:AEC Q100-001 AEC Q003, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:At appropriate time interval for each bonder to be used.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test E8 for Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage has been completely eliminated from the qualification requirements.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Table 3 outlines a superset of qualification tests required for evaluating new processes or process changes, serving as a baseline for supplier-user discussions, with the supplier responsible for justifying any test omissions.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, a note specifies that for certain part designs, particularly small packages, mounting the part may be necessary. This step ensures the structural integrity of the package is maintained throughout both the package opening process and the subsequent wire pull testing.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP C - PACKAGE ASSEMBLY INTEGRITY TESTS, STRESS:Solderability, ABV:SD, #:C3, NOTES:H, P, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:15, NUMBER OF LOTS:1, ACCEPT CRITERIA:>95% lead coverage, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-B102 or JEDEC J-STD-002D, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:If burn-in screening is normally performed on the device before shipment, samples for SD must first undergo burn-in. Perform 8 hour steam aging prior to testing (1 hour for Au-plated leads). The customer can request justification for using dry bake in place of steam aging.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, regarding HAST versus UHAST, it is noted that bias does have an effect on failure rate and may be used to accelerate testing if the component allows for higher bias, such as in cases involving corrosion or mobile ions.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Appendix 5 outlines criteria for EMC testing candidacy, targeting digital technologies like microprocessors and high-speed ICs that may produce radiated emissions interfering with communication receivers.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the NOTICE clarifies that AEC documents aim to eliminate misunderstandings in the automotive electronics industry, facilitate product interchangeability, and are adopted without regard to potential patents.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, generic data must be based on a matrix linking device characteristics and manufacturing processes, as detailed in Table 3 and Appendix 1, and data containing failures is unusable unless corrective action is documented and accepted.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a mission profile is defined as the comprehensive collection of all relevant environmental and functional loads that a semiconductor component will be exposed to throughout its entire use lifetime.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP D - DIE FABRICATION RELIABILITY TESTS, STRESS:Time Dependent Dielectric Breakdown, ABV:TDDB, #:D2, NOTES:—, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:—, NUMBER OF LOTS:—, ACCEPT CRITERIA:—, TEST METHOD:—, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:The data, test method, calculations and internal criteria should be available to the user upon request for new technologies.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS (continued), STRESS:Power Temperature Cycling, ABV:PTC, #:A5 alt, DATA TYPE:1, NOTES:D1G1T1U1W, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-A-105, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:Perform PTC if ΔTJ≥100°C cannot be achieved with IOL. Tested per duration indicated for Timing Requirements in Table 2A. Parts powered and chamber cycled to insure ΔTJ≥100°C (not to exceed absolute maximum ratings). TEST before and after PTC as a minimum. See Section 2.4 for RDSon pass/fail limits.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, controlling manufacturing variation and achieving low PPM reliability are addressed through dedicated process controls and screening methods, as outlined in standards AEC-Q001 and AEC-Q002.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, when proposing the use of "family" data in the Qualification Test Plan, the plan must document how previously completed reliability testing fulfills the requirements of the specification. An approved copy of this plan must be included with each qualification submission.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Appendix 1 defines the criteria for grouping components into a qualification family, allowing data from all family members to be considered generically acceptable for qualifying a specific device.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the military reference document specified is MIL-STD-883, which outlines Test Methods and Procedures for Microelectronics.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Table 3 presents a matrix of appropriate qualification tests for any proposed part changes, applicable to both new processes and re-qualification; it is a superset for baseline discussions between supplier and user.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the attributes defining a wafer fab process for family qualification are listed, including process flow, layout design rules, number of masks, cell density, lithographic process, doping process, passivation material/thickness, oxidation process/thickness, and front/back metallization details.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the prescribed sample size is deemed sufficient for detecting intrinsic flaws related to component design, construction, or material that affect performance.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, the flow chart analysis yields three definitive conclusions: AEC-Q100 test conditions apply, mission-profile-specific test conditions may apply, or Robustness Validation may be applied with detailed Tier1-Manufacturer alignment.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, Test F1 for Part Average Testing has been modified, with its Additional Requirements section now providing specific guidance on statistical sample sizes and acceptance criteria.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods, TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS, STRESS:Temperature Cycling, ABV:TC, #:A4, DATA TYPE:1, NOTES:D_G1U_3, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3 Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-A-104 Appendix 6, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:1000 cycles (TA = minimum range of -55°C to maximum rated junction temperature, not to exceed 150°C). Can reduce duration to 400 cycles using TA (max) = 25°C over part maximum rated junction temperature or using TA(max) = 175°C if the maximum rated junction temperature is above 150°C. TEST before and after TC. See Section 2.4 for RDson pass/fail limits.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the legend for Table 2 includes Note P, which advises that consideration should be made for whether a test applies to a Smart Power part or should be substituted with an equivalent Q100 test, based on factors like logic/sensing on the die, application, switching speed, power dissipation, and pin count.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, Table 1 outlines requirements for applying available part test data to reduce the number of lots needed for qualification. It serves as a guideline for leveraging existing data to streamline the qualification process.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, production requirements mandate that all qualification parts be manufactured using the tooling and processes at the site intended for volume production deliveries, ensuring representativeness.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, the final entries in Table 2 include: the elimination of Test E8 (Electrothermally Induced Gate Leakage); the addition of a new Test E12 for Lead (Pb) Free qualification; updates to Tests F1 and F2 (Part Average Testing and Statistical Bin/Yield Analysis) with modified guidance on sample sizes and accept criteria; and a modification to Test G1 (Mechanical Shock) regarding sample size per lot and the number of lots required.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, the assembly process attributes consist of leadframe base material, leadframe plating (internal/external), die attach material/method, wire bond material/diameter/process, and the plastic mold compound or other encapsulation material.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, a 'worst case' family requalification with appropriate tests is mandated whenever there is a change to the process or a material, with guidelines for this process provided in Table A1.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
In TEST GROUP G - CAVITY PACKAGE INTEGRITY TESTS of Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), for the item where the STRESS in the first column is Die Shear, its ABV is DS, # is G7, NOTES is H, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT is 5, NUMBER OF LOTS is 1, ACCEPT CRITERIA is 0 Fails, TEST METHOD is MIL-STD-883 Method 2019, and ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS is To be performed before cap/seal for all cavity devices.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, generic data for qualification must include material details, functional specifications, and test results of devices, along with a rationale justifying the use of such generic data.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, for initial qualification, the supplier must provide Stress Test Qualification data, with references to Table 2 and Appendix 4 for specific requirements.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP B - ACCELERATED LIFETIME SIMULATION TESTS, STRESS:Early Life Failure Rate, ABV:ELFR, #:B2, NOTES:H, P, B, N, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:800, NUMBER OF LOTS:3, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:AEC Q100-008, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:Devices that pass this stress can be used to populate other stress tests. Generic data is applicable. TEST before and after ELFR at room and hot temperature.

Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP C - PACKAGE ASSEMBLY INTEGRITY TESTS, STRESS:Wire Bond Pull Strength, ABV:WBP, #:C3, DATA TYPE:3, NOTES:D⊥G⊥E, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:10 bonds from min of 5 parts, NUMBER OF LOTS:10 bonds from min of 5 parts, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:MIL-STD-750-2 Method 2037 for Au and Al wire AEC Q006 for Cu wire, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:Condition C or D. For Au wire diameter >1mil, minimum pull strength after TC = 3 grams. For Au wire diameter <1mil, refer to MIL-STD-750-2 Method 2037 as a guideline for minimum pull strength. In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document, Section 1 SCOPE defines the document as containing a set of failure mechanism based stress tests that set minimum qualification requirements for integrated circuits (ICs), aiming to accelerate failures compared to use conditions.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, a qualification example specifies that three lots from a single FAB family, in any package outline, are required for High Temperature Reverse Bias (HTRB), High Temperature Gate Bias (HTGB), and H3TRB/HAST stress tests.

AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP B - ACCELERATED LIFETIME SIMULATION TESTS, STRESS:AC blocking voltage, ABV:ACBV, #:B1a, DATA TYPE:1, NOTES:DxGxPxUxY, SAMPLE SIZE /LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3 Note B, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:MIL-STD-750-1 M1040 condition A, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:1000 hours at the maximum AC blocking voltage and junction temperature specified in the user/supplier specification. The ambient temperature TA is to be adjusted to compensate for current leakage. TEST before and after ACBV as a minimum.

In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, failures caused by mishandling like EOS or ESD, or other non-reliability-related causes, must be discounted from reliability assessments but still reported as part of the data submission.
In the AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document file, supplier identification details, including the supplier name and contact information, are mandatory for traceability and communication purposes.

In the AEC_Q101_Rev_E_Base_Document file, manufacturing variation failures (low ppm issues) are addressed through proper process controls and screens as described in AEC-Q001 and -Q002, rather than through the qualification sample size.

AEC_Q100_Rev_H_Base_Document :
Table 2: Qualification Test Methods (continued), TEST GROUP A - ACCELERATED ENVIRONMENT STRESS TESTS (CONTINUED), STRESS:Temperature Cycling, ABV:TC, #:A4, NOTES:H, P, B, D, G, SAMPLE SIZE / LOT:77, NUMBER OF LOTS:3, ACCEPT CRITERIA:0 Fails, TEST METHOD:JEDEC JESD22-A104 and Appendix 3, ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:PC before TC for surface mount devices. Grade 0: -55°C to +150°C for 2000 cycles or equivalent. Grade 1: -55°C to +150°C for 1000 cycles or equivalent.
